keyVerseDR: "In humility, let each esteem others better than themselves." (Phil 2:3)

level1.title: This Week's Catholic Virtue: Humility
level1.story: Humility means not bragging or needing to be the center of attention. Every gift comes from God!
level1.heartIntro: Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice humility all week. On Saturday, talk together, write what you practiced, and a parent signs.
questions: When did we let someone else shine this week?
actions: Hang this sheet on the fridge
level1.prayer: Jesus, meek and humble of heart, make my heart like Yours. Amen.

activity.title: Daily Action Checklist
activity.intro: Color a star each day, Monday through Saturday. Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice with your family. A parent signs at the end of the week.
items: MON: Let someone else go first
TUE: Clap for someone else's success
THU: Say thank you when you get help
FRI: Do a hidden good deed
SAT: Thank God for your talents

level2.title: This Week's Catholic Virtue: Humility
level2.story: Humility means not boasting, not always seeking the spotlight, and not thinking we are more special than others. A humble person knows that every talent is a gift from God and is happy to let others shine. Saint Paul says to think of others as more important than ourselves. Jesus, the Son of God, was humble: He was born in a stable and washed feet.
level2.heartIntro: Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice humility all week. On Saturday, talk together, write what you practiced, and a parent signs.
questions: When did we let someone else shine this week?
How did God help us grow in humility?
actions: Hang this sheet on the fridge
